# Survey Dock Layouts and the Workstation beyond the rewrite epics

## Context

This is a survey leaf of #14800. It follows the [survey method](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/14800#issuecomment-5792321883) (@tobiu, 2026-09-23: the window is roughly 1,500 PRs and the split moved the Brain and the Fleet Manager out of scope).

This leaf covers the **dock** slice: 344 merged PRs, listed in the first comment. It holds PRs scoped `dock`, `dashboard` or `workstation` and, for PRs whose title names no scope, those touching `src/dashboard/` or a dock or Workstation app or example.

## The Problem

Chapter 1 of the draft ("Dock Layouts, built and then rebuilt", PR #19091) was written from eight rewrite epics (97 leaves) and the July tear-out deposit. The rest of the slice has not been read:
- the July showcase and tear-out PRs outside the epics;
- Workstation app work outside #18456;
- dock examples;
- fixes since #18303 closed.

The chapter cannot yet claim to be the dock story rather than the epics' story.

## The Architectural Reality

The population rule and the Tier 1–3 rubric are in the method comment. Chapter 1's timeline and package table are the baseline to extend, not to repeat.

## The Fix

Read the slice and keep its ledger on this issue: the population with every re-home disposed, and the partition. The public prose lands through the Dock chapter's live vehicle — PR #19121 rewrote the chapter under #19120's register (operator, 2026-09-23: no survey counts, partitions or nominations in the note). Chapter corrections and curated reader beats are deposited here for that PR to fold, each with its PR anchor. No second PR onto the same file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 Every PR in the slice is read; the ledger comment on this issue states read / narrated / excluded with the reason and disposes every re-home. The counts live here, not in the notes.
- [ ] AC-2 The Dock chapter at #19121's head is confirmed or corrected against the full slice; each correction names its PR and is either folded by #19121 or answered on this issue.
- [ ] AC-3 Each reader beat offered is one line: what changed, who notices it, and its PR; the note carries beats as reader prose, never as an inventory.
- [ ] AC-4 Reviewed cross-family: the Dock chapter's review on #19121 by a non-GPT seat.

## Out of Scope

- The second-window design itself (D#18730), which the chapter only reports.
- Tier-2 items beyond noting them: the upgrade-path leaf owns them.

## Related

#14800 · PR #19091 · #17836 · #18303 · #18456 · #17540

### Corrections to the Dock chapter at #19121's head `54a634f9`

- **C1 — the arc's honest bounds are gone.** The `dev` chapter names the flagship tour's two open defects; the draft names none for Dock. Per #19120 AC-3 they stay beside the arc: #16498 (resident cards lose children after a window place-cycle restore — the F7 composition gate, open) and #17871 (the full tour can lose its pooled grid after the midpoint; a re-triage receipt lands today — keep it until it closes).
- **C2 — "A whole stack can come home" links #18715, the Windows guide.** The behaviour shipped in `#15501` (07-18, popup stacks return atomically) and `#18684` (09-14, live headers prepared for the whole-stack return). Cite the PRs; keep the guide as the reader's link.
- **C3 — what a consumer extends is unnamed.** `Neo.dashboard.DockWorkspace` landed a week before the cut (`#17545`, 08-22; the Workstation rode it the same day, `#17565`), and the cut carried it into `src/dashboard/dock/` as `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace` — the class a consumer extends with its panes and a handful of hooks. "Instead of carrying a second docking implementation (#18456)" reads as if the Workstation had one to remove; it had this host.
- **Confirmed, no change:** `#17841` as the cut; `#17845` / `#17849` / `#17858`; `#18119`'s 1.2 s hold; `#15444` / `#15478`; `#18387` / `#18595` / `#19054`; the pane-vs-`Panel` correction; `#18151` / `#18474` / `#18605` as ticket anchors.

### Reader beats the chapter does not carry

One line each — what changed, who notices, the PRs. Take what fits the prose; the rest is this ledger's.

- **B1 — six header actions on every dock tab, engine-owned:** lock, reload, pin (collapse to the edge rail), pop-out, maximize and close, focus-gated, with tooltips (`#17626`, `#17952`, `#17953`, `#17970`, `#17974`, `#17982`, `#18072`, `#18187`). A host adds its own (`#17879`) or hides an engine one without re-implementing it (`#18582`); a pane answers `dockReload()` and `dockLock()` for its content (`#17974`, `#18057`); one with no reload contract is recreated (`#17996`).
- **B2 — auto-hide rails that move:** a reveal slides in from its edge, retargets between items and slides back (`#14906`, `#18079`, `#18118`, `#18120`, `#18139`); a click into an iframe pane leaves it open (`#18081`); a rail item can be a lazy module loaded on first reveal (`#18063`).
- **B3 — drop previews show the outcome:** the indicator menu offers every placement (`#14974`); split and edge previews paint the region the pane will occupy (`#17873`, `#17930`); cross-window previews measure the real target (`#16134`); a paused pointer is not a departure (`#16522`).
- **B4 — motion on every commit:** FLIP for structural moves, tokenised transitions with a reduced-motion collapse, and an animating signal that tests and tours key off (`#14944`, `#14947`, `#14966`); maximize glides instead of snapping (`#18534`).
- **B5 — themed everywhere:** the dock reads 14 engine tokens from all five shipped themes (`#17293`, `#17613`); the rail tab and the splitter paint from the engine (`#17524`, `#17531`); the rail's measure is a token the consumer owns (`#17614`, `#17638`); the slot a torn-out pane vacates is a themed placeholder, not a black panel (`#18418`).
- **B6 — the detach is also a keyboard command** (`#15483`), so it works where a platform refuses pointer-born popups.
- **B7 — a restore reaches a live app** (`#18253`), brings back the tab you were on (`#18257`), the rail widths (`#18581`) and a pane that was away in a vessel (`#18904`); one refused step no longer strands the rest (`#18586`).
- **B8 — declared, not programmed:** items are created through semantic operations (`#18470`), Group batches take the fast path (`#18526`), maximize survives a Group projection (`#18472`), a docked pane is reachable by `reference` like any component (`#18536`).
- **B9 — the flagship:** twenty panes, a 100k-row grid, live feeds, native pop-outs, a topology bar with undo and redo depth, a theme reveal from the pointer, and a scripted tour that is also the film's screenplay (`#15146`, `#15471`, `#16328`, `#18127`, `#18546`, `#18560`, `#19054`); its cards size from their pane and degrade as a declared unit (`#16487`, `#16722`), its palette outranks the theme it sits under (`#17987`). The dock demos left the Fleet Manager app for `examples/dashboard` (`#17562`, `#17588`).
- **B10 — fixes a 13.2 user would have felt:** a drag-resize or a lock click no longer restages every header (`#18154`, `#18207`, `#18746`); a reordered tab keeps naming its own item (`#18660`) and a moved tab publishes its source removal (`#18026`); maximize fills the dock host, not the viewport (`#18124`, `#18339`); a close moves focus even on a Group (`#18602`); a pane rebuilt by reload keeps its motion (`#18447`); malformed zones fail closed (`#18005`, `#18024`); a destroyed workspace cancels its pending admissions (`#18323`); released overlays leave the parent vdom (`#19013`); "open in a new window" works in dist builds (`#18841`).
- **B11 — where to start reading:** the architecture guide (`#17515`) beside the adoption series and the tutorial the draft already links.

**Recommendation for the chapter:** B1, B2, B3 + B4 (one paragraph — you see the outcome before you commit, and the commit animates), B5 and B6 belong in the public prose; they are what a developer meets on day one, and none is a count. B7–B11 stay here unless a digest beat wants them. C1–C3 are corrections, not options.

**C4 — an upgrade-path line for "Coming from 13.1", found while reviewing PR #19125 (open, not merged; write it in the tense the cut warrants).** Under one canvas worker per window group, every app-side call into a canvas remote carries `windowId`, and `Neo.canvas.Base#setTheme` takes `{theme, windowId}` (Emmy's R3 on that PR asks the scalar form to keep working). A consumer-authored canvas component — one extending `Neo.app.SharedCanvas` or `Neo.component.Canvas` and calling its renderer without `windowId` — keeps working in one window and is refused as `NEO_UNROUTABLE` the moment a second window group exists (a second tab, a bookmark). The in-tree census guards the engine's own callers, not consumers'. Source: PR #19125's diff (`RemoteMethodAccess#generateRemote`, `CanvasGroups#resolve`) and #19103's ledger. Deposited for #19121's upgrade section; no action on this leaf.
